author: reek
body: `list-at`, `list-set-at` and `list-insert-at` trap on an index outside the list. This file is the other half: every LEGAL index must still answer, for all three, because the compiler reads `list-at` constantly and a guard that refuses a legal read would stop the compiler rather than a program.

author: reek
body: The traps themselves cannot be pinned here -- they are UD2, so the guest dies and there is no output to compare. `codex/test/list-oob-read.codex` and `codex/test/list-oob-write.codex` are those demonstrations and they carry a `.fatal`, which means each is a compile check plus a manual read. This file is the part a battery can fail on, so it is the one that has to be complete.

author: reek
body: Two boundaries are named because they point in opposite directions. `list-insert-at xs (list-length xs) v` is an APPEND and is legal -- the shift loop moves nothing and the store lands in the slot the length is about to grow into -- so the insert bound is `i <= len` where the read and write bounds are `i < len`. A guard copied from one to the other without reading the shift loop gets exactly this wrong, and `ins-end` below is the line that says so.

author: reek
body: The view rows -- a tail view is bounded by its own length, not the backing block's -- lived here until 2026-07-28 and are now `list-view-bounds`. The tail view comes from a Cons match, which the cross plugs refuse by design, and while the rows lived here the refusal took this file's six legal-index readings off both cross lanes with them. Split, this file runs everywhere the compiler does.
